checks: Old saves gain ten healthy components, existing damage survives, and new internal failures reload without damaging unrelated pistons.
Engine swaps and inactive-car sanitization do not transfer piston-only failures to a rotary or invent failed pistons.
All eight engine choices and four stock cars run; rotary diagnosis exposes housings and eccentric shaft without imaginary rods or timing chain.
Fuel pump and ignition failures cut native combustion and NOS without destroying internals; recovery, tuning and reload cannot bypass them.
Crushed intake reduces native air admission and boost, fuel-pump wear leans the native mixture, and exhaust obstruction creates measured shaft load work.
Cracked block and head leak independently; replacing the radiator or refilling does not heal either component.
Stuck thermostat causes heat and subsequent internal damage; cooling repairs preserve that damage and fluid loss.
Oil starvation and mechanical overrev damage crank and chain; a broken chain damages valves while turning, and chain replacement cannot repair them.
Front and rear impacts damage the corresponding engine and exhaust parts; diagnostic rows and warning messages name the faulty component.
Damaged intake and exhaust produce separate PCM targets tied to running state and mechanical volume; reset clears them.
limits: Lumped component model, not finite-element or calibrated real-car damage.
Timing loss uses misfires, valve-contact damage and combustion cut; no new tooth-by-tooth chain solver.
Exhaust restriction uses the native dissipative crank-load channel. Internal parts share engine/oil thermal nodes.
